bug_description: Database query performance degrades when processing large datasets. Queries that complete in 100ms with 1000 records take 5+ seconds with 100,000 records.

hypotheses.hypothesis_text: The absence of an index on the filter column will cause table scans, resulting in linear O(n) performance degradation as dataset size increases.

steps: Create test database with mock customer data (1M records, 50GB)
Create query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE region='NORTH' without index
Measure execution time 5 times, record average
Add index: CREATE INDEX idx_region ON customers(region)
Measure execution time 5 times, record average
independent_vars: Presence of index on filter column (true/false)
dependent_vars: Query plan type (Seq Scan vs Index Scan)

metadata.prediction: Adding an index on the filter column will reduce query execution time from 5+ seconds (100K records) to approximately 100ms, matching the performance with 1000 records. This will demonstrate the O(log n) vs O(n) performance difference.
